title: Introduction and personal background
description: Cathy Naugle records basic identifying details: Dawna Northrup, maiden name Nissen, her childhood nickname Donnie, and her birthdate. Dawna explains the family moved back to Lewiston from Colville, Washington, when she was about eleven, traveling by car with a small trailer holding everything they owned.

title: Parents' background and work
description: Dawna describes her mother, a Rasmussen born in Colville, who was mostly a homemaker but clerked, tended bar, and waited tables. Her stepfather Rex Nissen, raised near Bowles, Idaho, worked as a boilermaker and welder building tanks.

title: Marriage and children
description: Dawna tells of her former husband Russell, who manages a drugstore, their wedding in Moscow, and their three children Bob, David, and Karen born in Pocatello and Idaho Falls. She muses about hyphenating her maiden name if she remarries.

title: Schooling; skills and work history
description: Dawna recalls dropping out of high school after marrying at fifteen to babysit, then attending secretarial school after her divorce while pregnant with Karen. She lists her skills, carpentry on her own house, club involvement, buying her own house and car, and her jobs as a carhop, water purifier store manager, and secretary to a school superintendent.

title: Interests; small town versus city life
description: Dawna describes her reading tastes, embroidery, refinishing furniture, currently a biography of Carl Jung. She compares small-town living favorably with city life, citing friendliness and community connection, while noting neighbors' suspicion of a single woman and rural closeness to nature, gardening, and canning.

title: Family roles; childhood memories
description: Dawna contrasts her present life as a divorced head of household with her childhood home, recalling hauling water by bucket and doing the family ironing in fifth grade. She remembers Easter picnics, rodeos, sledding in Colville, and mischief with her friend Becky Miller, plus her parents' divorce and brief later contact with her real father.

title: Courtship, early marriage, and in-laws
description: Dawna explains she married Russell at fifteen to avoid moving again and lived with his crowded family, which overwhelmed her as an only child. She relates her teenage miscarriage, the confusing hospital experience with unfamiliar doctors, and the in-laws gathering around her bed.

title: Birth control; doctors; hopes for children
description: Dawna discusses planning and spacing her children, embarrassment about birth control, and praise for its availability to young people. She criticizes doctors who withhold explanations and tells of dismissing one who misdiagnosed her sore throat, then states her wish that her children choose fulfilling, independent lives.

title: Recreation and relaxation
description: Dawna talks about her leisure life: dancing, visiting friends, rafting on the Clearwater with another woman, camping alone in the woods, swimming, sledding with an Indian club outing, and staying indoors in winter. She notes she does not do much specifically with her seven-year-old daughter.

title: Parenting philosophy; daughter's independence and feminism; self-discovery reflection
description: Dawna Northrup describes her daughter Karen's fearlessness climbing on bridge cables during a camping trip at North Fork and her daughter's observation about gender inequality in Buddhist education. Northrup reflects on encouraging her daughter's independence and contrasts this with her own experience of early marriage and eight years supporting her family, expressing hope that her daughter will achieve self-sufficiency and self-discovery before taking on adult responsibilities.
